subject: Culture
title: Nowruz and the Persian New Year
description: A 60-second lesson on Nowruz and the Persian New Year.

hook.text: Nowruz has been celebrated for over 3,000 years. Empires fell, religions changed, but the holiday survived.

buildup.text: It marks the spring equinox. Families set a Haft-sin table with seven symbolic items starting with the letter S.

discovery.text: Nowruz survived the Arab conquest, the Mongol invasion, and even the Iranian Revolution's attempt to suppress it.

twist.text: Today over 300 million people celebrate Nowruz. It's observed from the Balkans to Central Asia.

climax.text: A festival that outlasts empires carries something deeper than tradition. It carries identity.

punchline.text: Three thousand years and still counting.

quiz.question: What astronomical event does Nowruz align with?

details.summary: Nowruz — the Persian New Year celebrated at the spring equinox — predates Islam by over 2,500 years and is observed by 300 million people across Iran, Central Asia, and diaspora communities. Its Haft-sin table of seven symbolic items represents hope, rebirth, and continuity.
details.whyItMatters: Nowruz is one of the world's oldest continuously celebrated festivals. Its survival through Arab conquest, Mongol invasion, and Islamic reform shows the extraordinary resilience of cultural traditions.
takeaways: Nowruz has been celebrated for over 3,000 years
It marks the spring equinox — the astronomical new year
The Haft-sin table displays seven items beginning with the letter S

faq.question: What is the Haft-sin table?
faq.answer: The Haft-sin displays seven items starting with the Persian letter sin (S): sabzeh (sprouts, rebirth), samanu (sweet paste, affluence), senjed (dried fruit, love), sir (garlic, medicine), sib (apple, beauty), somaq (sumac, sunrise), serkeh (vinegar, patience).

faq.question: How has Nowruz survived so many conquests?
faq.answer: Nowruz survived Arab-Islamic conquest because it was too deeply rooted to eradicate. Various Islamic rulers tried to suppress it but gave up. Its connection to the astronomical equinox gives it a scientific basis beyond religion. UNESCO recognized Nowruz as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009.
